Detailed Description

Stateful, deterministic-when-seeded live match simulation in real match time: in watch mode one simulated second is one second of the match (a full match with stoppages and added time is roughly 5,900 simulated seconds). Play mode can accelerate the match clock while body/ball physics retain the same timestep; see setPlayHalfMinutes().

update() uses a fixed internal timestep, so the same seed produces the same match at different render frame rates. Home attacks toward x=1 and away attacks toward x=0. The engine is copyable, which highlight prediction uses to look ahead deterministically.

Strategies and simulation state are owned by value. Player pointers and the StatsConfig reference are borrowed: keep them alive and unchanged for the engine's lifetime, including any prediction copies and worker batches. The engine records match consequences; the career applies them afterwards. See docs/development/match-engine.md for the step order and extension map, and docs/development/player-behavior.md for movement and action selection.

◆ ContestMeet

enum class MatchEngine::ContestMeet : std::uint8_t
strongprivate

The tackler has played the owner's ball inside both reaches: both feet's cooldowns (rows 1, 2 and 5 of the step 2 table). What a contest touch meets (tackling plan, the step 2 table as step 4 left it).

Enumerator
UNOPPOSED 

Rows 1 and 2: the tackler's touch alone (the carrier recovering, or swinging at nothing).

BLOCK_COMMITTED 

Row 3: the carrier's planned touch in the same moment: a block.

BLOCK_REACTING 

Row 5: the carrier's foot free, his touch not due: it reacts, a wall: a block.

Presentation helper for the live view: advances the match by wallSeconds of wall-clock time according to the playback mode. In HIGHLIGHTS mode it skips (simulates headless, never dropping steps) to the start of the next predicted highlight window and then plays the window at the highlight speed. ◆ applyScenario()

bool MatchEngine::applyScenario ( const MatchScenario &  scenario,
MatchState  scenarioState = MatchState::PLAYING,
float  scenarioMatchTime = 0.0F,
int  scenarioHomeScore = 0,
int  scenarioAwayScore = 0 
)

Loads a fully-specified deterministic scenario and evaluates the carrier's decision exactly as the live engine would (no physics step is advanced). The renderer never calls this; it is only an explicit headless evaluation hook for the scenario suite. The optional parameters let scenario tests reproduce late-game and score-state behaviour deterministically. A controlled carrier (setControlledPlayer, already applied by a step) makes no AI decision and waits for his input.

void MatchEngine::forcePass ( PlayerID  playerId,
PlayerID  receiverId,
ForcedPassStyle  style 
)

Drills: the player passes to receiverId, through the AI's own pass (its target, lead and weight), as soon as he has the ball and can act; style can force it along the ground or lofted. Logged and replayed.

◆ forcePassTo()

void MatchEngine::forcePassTo ( PlayerID  playerId,
PitchPoint  spot,
ForcedPassStyle  style,
std::optional< BallSpin >  spin = std::nullopt,
std::optional< float >  arrivalSpeed = std::nullopt,
bool  firstTime = false 
)

Drills: the player passes to spot (metres), with nobody there, as soon as he has the ball and can act: weighted as for a man standing on it, and a lofted pass is aimed to land on it; spin is the spin he means (PassOption::spin), arrivalSpeed its pace there. firstTime: a pass played to him he plays on as it reaches him, without a touch (a ground ball, Binturong body; otherwise after his touch, as usual). Logged and replayed.

void MatchEngine::forceShot ( PlayerID  playerId,
std::optional< Vector2F >  aim = std::nullopt,

)

◆ forceTackleIntent()

void MatchEngine::forceTackleIntent ( PlayerID  playerId,
TackleIntent  intent 
)

Drills: the next header the player wins goes to spot (metres; SPOT), at goalAim in the goal (metres across from the middle and up; GOAL), or is cushioned and kept (KEEP), instead of what the brain would choose. Logged and replayed. Drills: from now on the player's tackles on a free ball (an opponent's ball outside his reach) mean intent, instead of the control touch (tackling plan step 3; the brain chooses in step 5). Logged and replayed.

◆ setControlledPlayer()

bool MatchEngine::setControlledPlayer ( PlayerID  playerId)

Play-mode seam: hands one outfield player to an external controller from the next fixed step (0 hands him back to the AI). While controlled, the player moves by the stick (at MatchTuning::Control::PHYSICS_SUBSTEPS per step, with the same acceleration, braking, turning and fatigue model) and acts only on the action button; team-mates and opponents stay AI. Set pieces and goalkeeping remain AI-driven. A controlled player who is substituted, sent off or goes in goal hands control back to the AI. Returns false (and changes nothing) for goalkeepers and players not on the pitch.

◆ setDrillTarget()

void MatchEngine::setDrillTarget ( PlayerID  playerId,
std::optional< PitchPoint >  target,
bool  urgent,
const std::vector< PitchPoint > &  route = {},
float  apexOffsetMetres = 0.0F,
float  outwardRoomMetres = 0.0F,
std::optional< float >  facing = std::nullopt,
bool  atSpeed = false 
)

Drills: holds a player's tactical target (metres), which then replaces the planner's; urgent makes him run at it flat out. A route gives up to two waypoints on the way, and his line through them: how far inside each the turn's apex may pass (apexOffsetMetres; negative is outside) and how far out the line may be pushed to widen it (outwardRoomMetres). facing asks his body to face that way (an angle like facingAngle) whichever way he moves. atSpeed: he means to reach it at full speed (running through it), not stop on it. No target releases him to the planner. Logged and replayed like any manager change.

◆ strikeStillBall()

bool MatchEngine::strikeStillBall ( PlayerID  playerId)

Drills: the player shoots, through the AI's own shot, as soon as he has the ball and can act; with aim, at that spot in the goal instead of one he picks (metres: across from the goal's centre, + toward pitch y = 1, and height); with powerShare, struck at that share of his shot power (Binturong body) instead of the usual; firstTime: off a pass to him, struck as it reaches him without a touch (a ground ball, Binturong body; otherwise after his touch). Logged and replayed. Drills (game xG plan): the player, holding a still ball (startDrill with him as the carrier), strikes it where it lies at once: an open-play shot at the spot his brain picks, struck by his body as a dead ball, with no touch or step before it (the ball isn't put at his feet first, as it is for forceShot). Call it after startDrill, before the first step. False if he doesn't have the ball. Logged and replayed.
